newsitem.title: ITALY: BASKETBALL-RIVERS LEADS OLYMPIAKOS TO FINAL AGAINST BARCELONA.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-RIVERS LEADS OLYMPIAKOS TO FINAL AGAINST BARCELONA.

text.p: David Rivers scored 28 points to lead Olympiakos to their third European basktetball championship final in four years on Tuesday when they beat Ljubljana of Slovenia 74-65 in the semifinals of the Final Four tournament.
Their opponents on Thursday will be Barcelona who overcame a nervous spell to defeat Villeurbanne of France 77-70.
Barcelona were narrowly beaten in last year's final and Olympiakos lost in the final in both 1994 and 1995 so on Thursday one of them must at last come good in Europe's top club event.
Roared on by 5,500 fervent supporters, Olympiakos led all the way against gallant opponents making their debut in a Final Four event.
Playmaker Rivers, formerly with the Los Angeles Lakers, was on top of his game for Olympiakos, weaving his way around the court and popping up with important points at just the right time.
Dragan Tarlac and Franco Nakic, both on 10, were the only other Olympiakos men to reach double figures.

Ljubljana's top scorer was Vladimir Stepania on 12, but the player to catch the eye was guard Dusan Hauptman, the oldest man in the tournament at 36. He was an inspiration to his young team mates, scoring 10 points and leading by example.
Olympiakos turned in a measured performance, generally holding a comfortable five or six-point advantage.
But the defining moment came with three minutes left when Rivers, after some near-exhibition stuff, burst through to score two more points, despite shooting off balance and tumbling to the floor.
That gave Olympiakos a 10-point cushion and there was no way back for the Slovenian champions, whose vociferous following was outnumbered 10-1 by the Greek supporters.
Coach Dusan Ivkovic, at last able to call on a full roster after various injuries, said: "We played a good game. Everything went well. We were good at rebounds and fast breaks."
Ljubljana coach Zmago Sagadin singled out Rivers as a key factor. "Olympiakos are a more experienced team and this was obvious at the most important moments."
Barcelona led most of the way in the second semifinal but Villeurbanne threatened when they fought back to take the lead for the first time on 63-62 with just under five minutes left.
Cheered on by the Olympiakos fans, preferring a final against the less fancied French team, Villeurbanne looked briefly as if they might spring a surprise.

But shaven-headed Serb Sasha Djordjevic, who has transformed Barcelona's season since arriving in January, scored a vital two-pointer followed by two coolly-taken penalties to tip the balance back again.
It was tough luck on Villeurbanne's Brian Howard and Delaney Rudd, who both scored 20 points and did everything asked of them.
Djordjevic was Barcelona's top scorer on 17 with guard Xavier Fernandez contributing 14.
